Destination captures live after synchronizing req, so it can capture a later payload or a changing asynchronous word instead of the accepted send payload. Request and acknowledgment form a two-stage toggle handshake, but live updates on every source edge while the request is outstanding. The destination therefore captures a later value, or a changing asynchronous word, rather than a payload held for the accepted send. A source can send one value and change payload_in before rq reaches its second stage, yielding a concrete protocol counterexample without assuming unusual clocks. Input-delay constraints impose no hold contract. Reset and bundled-data physical timing are separate obligations.
